decision.reason: Shipped row 435 represents Loftus, Miller, & Burns (1978, 10.1037/0278-7393.4.1.19) Experiment 3 (1-day delayed postevent misinformation condition), tested in Studies 1 and 2 and adjudicated in canonical adjudications/f915a8798237e4f0.json. In Study 3 (Reversed Order Study, N=221, pages 11-13; preregistered at https://osf.io/y75c8/), Wiechert et al. (2025) empirically retest the reversed-order misinformation procedure (presenting the cowitness narrative in Session 1, one day before the original accident video and recognition test in Session 2) to adjudicate between single-trace/blocking and activation-based multiple-trace accounts. Study 3 found a nonsignificant, Bayesian-inconclusive difference between misled (58.40%) and control (67.10%) conditions (chi-square(1) = 1.21, p = .272, Cramer's V = 0.09, BF01 = 1.65). The Introduction (page 3) states that the authors replicated the reversed-order procedure, citing Rantzen & Markham (1992, 10.1080/00221309.1992.9921156), and the General Discussion (page 14) contrasts Study 3's null result with both Lindsay & Johnson (1989) and Rantzen & Markham (1992). However, prior v1 review and Luna erred in counting both co-cited papers as separate missing rows from distinct DOIs alone. Primary context 0097 shows that Rantzen & Markham (1992) cites Lindsay & Johnson (1989) in Crossref metadata, but both originals are primary-body and abstract inaccessible. Without primary access to either original's published findings and conditions, actual evidence cannot determine whether Rantzen & Markham (1992) is the single closest replication-chain link or whether Study 3 independently retests one versus both originals.
